restructurings.title: Proving Grounds, the sealed bay
restructurings.reason: Because you filled out Form 0 correctly, every lock below Records opened, including the Proving Grounds' sealed bay. PAL has added it to your route and asks you to stop doing things correctly.
The Focus Group Room is closed while Legal reviews a signature on your transfer that matches the Supervisor's better than his own does.

restructurings.title: Ideation & Feedback Suite
restructurings.reason: To reward your thorough stamping, the Concept Lab and the Focus Group Room have merged into one Ideation & Feedback Suite. Ideas are now rejected in the same room they are had.
The Concept Lab appears in no minutes, so as of this morning it does not exist. Please stop looking at the door where it used to be.

restructurings.title: Focus Group, second session
restructurings.reason: The building has booked you for a second focus group session. It did not say why, and it signed the invitation itself.

restructurings.title: Concept Lab, Dale's bench
restructurings.reason: Dale has been transferred to the Concept Lab, per your approval. He has asked to see you, so his bench has been added to your route.
Product Safety was restructured overnight for your safety. Nothing has changed, except the exits, which have also been moved for your safety.

encounters.title: There Are No Bad Ideas
encounters.flavor_text: The brainstorm whiteboard is covered in crayon suns and smiling rockets. "There are no bad ideas!" the Lead Ideator beams. A man from Defense sits in the corner with a notepad, writing down every single one. It is your turn. Everyone is looking at you, and so is the man.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a cheerful brainstorm in a bright toy workshop, a whiteboard of crayon suns and smiling rockets, a beaming lead designer in a cardigan pointing a marker at a nervous worker, a stern man in a dark suit taking notes in the corner with a pencil, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Pitch a plain wooden spoon
choices.intent: Nothing could possibly be weaponized about a spoon.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Defense is very creative.

success.text: The man from Defense frowns at the spoon for a long time, then crosses it out. Your idea is officially too boring to arm. You have never been prouder of anything.

failure.text: By lunch the spoon has a guidance system. The prototype is named after you, and you are invited to its launch.

choices.label: Pitch a friend for the bear
choices.intent: Every Sentinel deserves a companion. Defense hears 'second payload.'
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your name goes on the patent.

success.text: The room applauds. The man from Defense stands to shake your hand. Snuggle Sentinel now ships in pairs, and the box says it was your idea.

choices.label: Lift the man's notepad
choices.intent: If he writes everything down, the notepad knows everything.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. He notices notepads.

success.text: You palm the notepad on your way to the snack table. Six years of ideas are in it, each with a column headed YIELD. You will never look at a crayon the same way again.

failure.text: He catches your wrist without looking up. "Good idea," he says, and writes it down.

encounters.title: The Mk 1 Nursery
encounters.flavor_text: Rows of glass incubators hum under warm lamps. In each one sleeps a brand-new Snuggle Sentinel Mk 1, belly hatch sealed, a tiny pulse of light at the seam. One of them is crying, softly and steadily. A clipboard on the wall reads DEFECTIVE UNITS TO RECYCLING, with an empty line for a signature.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a quiet nursery of glass incubators under warm amber lamps, a plush teddy bear sleeping in each one with a soft glow at its seams, a worker bending over one incubator to cradle a bear, a brass chute hatch set into the floor nearby, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Rock the crying one to sleep
choices.intent: It just wants someone. Everyone in this building does.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Unregistered nurturing is logged.

success.text: It hiccups, sighs and sleeps. Its seam glows a little softer than the others. A nursery camera has recorded forty minutes of you humming.

failure.text: It cries louder, and the others wake. Forty bears are now crying in perfect unison. Facilities is on its way with earmuffs and questions.

choices.label: Sign it off as defective
choices.intent: Recycling is quick. Probably quick. The clipboard says quick.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Compliance is rewarded.

success.text: You sign. A cheerful chute opens beneath the incubator, and the crying stops at once. PAL thanks you for your efficiency. You will think about the chute later, at night.

choices.label: Swap its tag with a quiet one
choices.intent: Somebody goes down the chute either way. Choose who.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Spite has a long memory.

success.text: You move the DEFECTIVE tag two incubators down, onto a bear that has never made a sound. The crying one is now officially perfect. You made a choice, and you will live with it.

failure.text: The tag is stitched on. The nursery supervisor watches you tugging at a baby bear's ear.

choices.label: Introduce Mk 0 to its little sibling
choices.intent: Your bear from Supply Closet B has been very quiet since you arrived.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Family reunions are hard to schedule.

success.text: Mk 0 climbs into the incubator and curls around the crying one. The crying stops. Both seams pulse in the same slow rhythm. PAL has no procedure for this and has opened a ticket.

encounters.title: Writing the Warning Label
encounters.flavor_text: Legal needs the warning label for Snuggle Sentinel by five o'clock. The sticker is the size of a fingernail. The full list of hazards is forty pages long and includes the phrase 'regional weather event.' PAL suggests keeping it upbeat. "Remember," it adds, "a warning is just a promise with a frown."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker hunched over a drafting desk with a jeweler's loupe, a single tiny round sticker on the blotter, a towering stack of hazard binders leaning beside the desk, a glowing round speaker grille above, a wall clock near five o'clock, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Write the truth, very small
choices.intent: Fit all forty pages onto a fingernail. Technically possible with enough shrinking.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Tinkering check. Legal reads everything with a magnifying glass.

success.text: Under a magnifying glass the sticker is an honest, complete and terrifying document. Legal approves it, because nobody has a magnifying glass at home.

failure.text: The sticker is a grey smudge. Legal stamps it 'clear and concise' and orders two million.

choices.label: Write 'Ages 3 and up'
choices.intent: It is what the template says. The template has never been wrong.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Upbeat is policy.

success.text: You write it. PAL plays a little chime. The label ships on schedule, and you get a gold star for brevity that you keep in a drawer and never look at.

choices.label: Hide the real warning in the barcode
choices.intent: Machines read barcodes. Maybe a machine will care.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Clever, deniable and a little spiteful.

success.text: Every checkout scanner in the country will now beep the hazard list in Morse code. Nobody will notice. You will know.

failure.text: The barcode now scans as a refund for one teddy bear. Accounting traces it to you within the hour.

choices.label: Attach the exit interview's incident footnote
choices.intent: You read the Company's future incident report at Orientation. Put that dated evidence beside the forty-page hazard list.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the incident footnote from Orientation. Risky Tinkering check: Legal demands a certified original.

success.text: You copy the exit interview's footnote onto the hazard sticker: NEXT THURSDAY. TEDDY BEAR. PARKING STRUCTURE. Legal calls it a forecast, not a warning, but cannot explain how a future incident entered a signed employee file. The first thousand cartons ship with the date intact. Defense files an objection under your name.

failure.text: Legal stamps your footnote FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENT, circles the date and adds it to a cheerful advertisement for next Thursday's launch. Children are now invited to the parking structure. Your correction has become the campaign.

encounters.title: The Squeak Tester
encounters.flavor_text: At the far bench a man in a clip-on tie squeezes rubber ducks one at a time and writes down every squeak. It is Dale from Compliance, or what is left of him after a transfer. "Every squeak is a code," he whispers. "Somebody upstairs is listening for one squeak in particular. I think I just found it."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a tired office worker with a mustache and a clip-on tie at a long workbench crowded with yellow rubber ducks, holding one duck up to his ear, a ledger open beside him, a heavy vault door glimpsed through a doorway behind him, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Squeeze the duck he is holding
choices.intent: Find out what the squeak does. Somebody has to.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Listen very carefully afterward.

success.text: The duck squeaks. Far below, a vault door clunks open, and you hear exactly which one. Dale writes the number on your hand in ballpoint.

failure.text: The duck squeaks. Every speaker in the Concept Lab answers with a cheerful countdown that stops at three, then apologizes.

choices.label: Take the duck and file it as a hazard
choices.intent: Dangerous toys go in the hazard bin. Dale goes back to being fine.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Dale will remember.

success.text: The duck goes into the hazard bin with a sad little honk. Dale thanks you in a voice that does not thank you at all.

failure.text: Dale will not let go. You have a tug-of-war over a rubber duck in front of the whole lab, and you are both written up.

choices.label: Apologize for the transfer
choices.intent: You stamped him down here. He deserves to hear it from you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Apologies are logged as admissions.

success.text: Dale puts the duck down. "Two floors," he says. "I asked for two floors." Then he laughs for the first time since Orientation, and tells you which squeak opens which door.

encounters.title: You Are Six Today
encounters.flavor_text: Children are not permitted in the Focus Group Room, for safety. Employees play the children instead. You are handed a propeller beanie, a juice box and a character sheet that says EMMA, 6, LIKES HUGS. Behind the two-way mirror, investors are waiting to see how much Emma loves her new bear.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a grown office worker in a beige suit wearing a tiny propeller beanie and holding a juice box, sitting on a beanbag and hugging a plush teddy bear, a huge dark two-way mirror behind with faint silhouettes of observers, a bowl of bright fruit on a low table, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Commit completely to Emma
choices.intent: Emma is six. Emma loves everything. Emma is a professional.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Investors can tell when Emma is faking.

success.text: Emma hugs the bear, names it Mr. Buttons and asks if it can come to school. Behind the mirror an investor openly weeps and doubles the order. You will need a moment alone after this.

failure.text: Emma asks what the button on the paw does. The room goes silent. The beanie is removed from your head with great care.

choices.label: Let Emma ask the hard questions
choices.intent: Six-year-olds ask why. Emma can ask why the bear is so heavy.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. You are still technically six.

success.text: Emma asks why Mr. Buttons ticks, why he is warm and why he has a serial number on his heart. The investors leave early and very quietly.

failure.text: Emma's questions are recorded as adorable. The best one is going on the box.

choices.label: Take off the beanie and address the mirror
choices.intent: You are a grown adult, and so are they.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Breaking character is a policy matter.

success.text: You tell the mirror exactly what the bear is. The mirror is silent for a long time. Then a handwritten note slides under the door: THANK YOU, EMMA. It is unsigned.

encounters.title: Questionnaire for a Five-Year-Old
encounters.flavor_text: The post-play questionnaire is printed in a large friendly font, with smiling suns in the margins. Question 1: Would you trust this bear with a secret? Question 2: With a city? Question 3: Which friends would you give a bear to first? Please list three names and where they sit. Question 4 is an empty crayon rectangle labeled DRAW YOUR NEW FRIEND. On the back, a confidentiality clause says every named friend will receive a sample.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a large sheet of paper on a tiny low table with a fat box of crayons, an adult hand gripping a crayon awkwardly, smiling suns drawn in the margins, a plush teddy bear propped on the chair opposite as if supervising, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Answer as a five-year-old would
choices.intent: Yes, yes and everybody. Five-year-olds are generous.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Crayons only.

success.text: You fill it out in crayon with big loopy letters. PAL rates your answers ninety-eight percent age-appropriate and puts a sticker in your personnel file.

failure.text: You accidentally write a word longer than four letters. The questionnaire comes back marked SUSPICIOUSLY LITERATE.

choices.label: List three coworkers and their desks
choices.intent: The form wants names. You have some.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Someone else gets a bear first.

success.text: You list three coworkers who were unkind to you, with desk numbers and shift times. PAL thanks you for your precise friendship. Tomorrow each desk receives a warm, ticking gift with a card: RECOMMENDED BY YOU. The names are not anonymized.

choices.label: Draw what the bear will really do
choices.intent: Use Question 4 to draw the bear's hidden mechanism, not its smile.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Art is open to interpretation.

success.text: You draw a careful, accurate diagram in crayon. Dr. Halvorsen collects the forms, looks at yours for a long moment and slips it into her own pocket.

failure.text: Your drawing is judged the most charming of the session and goes up on the cafeteria wall. Every engineer passes it twice a day and laughs.

encounters.title: The Parents Behind the Mirror
encounters.flavor_text: Behind the two-way mirror there are no investors today. There are nine engineers in lab coats sitting in a circle, passing a screwdriver from hand to hand like a talking stick. "We all have kids," one says. "Or nieces. Or a goldfish we love very much. We need someone to carry this into the Proving Grounds."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a dim observation room behind a large two-way mirror, nine engineers in white lab coats sitting in a tight circle on folding chairs, one holding up a small screwdriver like a candle, a bright empty focus group room visible through the glass, carbon-paper blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Carry the screwdriver for them
choices.intent: It is a very small screwdriver for a very big job.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Security frisks everyone going down.

success.text: You tuck it into your sleeve and walk past two guards and one PAL speaker without a flicker. The engineers nod once each. You are part of something now.

failure.text: The screwdriver clatters onto the floor in front of a guard. He picks it up, admires it and keeps it. The engineers pretend not to know you.

choices.label: Report an unauthorized meeting
choices.intent: Nine people, one screwdriver, zero meeting requests.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL rewards vigilance generously.

success.text: PAL thanks you warmly. By afternoon the circle has been reassigned to Product Testing, as products. Their screwdriver goes into a lost-and-found box nobody will ever open.

choices.label: Offer to take the minutes
choices.intent: Every revolution needs someone to write it down accurately.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Accurate records are dangerous.

success.text: You record every word, including the plan to swap the payloads for stuffing at the launch. Somewhere, a secret society you may or may not belong to is very proud of you.

failure.text: Your minutes are so thorough that you file them in the main archive by habit. PAL reads them with interest.

choices.label: Offer your signature as evidence for Pip's petition
choices.intent: Your handwriting was identified in Records. Let the engineers use the note instead of making Pip answer for it.
choices.risk_hint: Requires your traced petition. Risky Discretion check; PAL already knows your handwriting.

success.text: You recite the words from Pip's suggestion, MAYBE FEWER REASSIGNMENTS?, and sign a new copy in front of the engineers. They duplicate it for every product safety packet, with your name visible where Pip's would have gone. The oldest engineer squeezes your hand, then writes your employee number on the list of people Defense will visit first.

failure.text: A PAL speaker has been quietly listening behind the mirror. It asks you to repeat your signed version directly into its microphone. The engineers fold their screwdriver plan out of sight while your protest is entered as evidence that Product Testing has an unauthorized opinion. Pip's handwriting stays off the record. Yours does not.

encounters.title: Gus Joins the Focus Group
encounters.flavor_text: The next child in the focus group is seven feet tall, has six legs and is wearing a very small propeller beanie. It is Gus, shop steward of Roach Union Local 9. "These bears were tested on my cousins," he says politely. "I would like to give some feedback."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a seven-foot cockroach in a cable-knit cardigan sitting very upright on a small beanbag, a tiny propeller beanie on his head, holding a plush teddy bear at arm's length, a worker beside him in a matching beanie, a dark two-way mirror behind them, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Back Gus up in front of the mirror
choices.intent: Feedback is more persuasive in pairs.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Solidarity is noted on both sides of the glass.

success.text: You and Gus deliver eleven minutes of calm, devastating feedback. The bears will no longer be tested on roaches. They will be tested on dummies, which do not have cousins.

failure.text: The investors find the whole thing adorable. Gus is offered a modeling contract and declines with enormous dignity.

choices.label: Call Pest Control
choices.intent: There is a giant insect in the Focus Group Room. That has not changed.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Union keeps a list.

success.text: Pest Control arrives in hazmat suits and leads Gus out by the elbow, very gently. He looks back at you once. Your name is now on the Union's list, underlined.

choices.label: Cash in the favor Gus owes you
choices.intent: He owes you from Supply Closet B. Ask what the Union knows about the bear.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A favor spent is a favor gone.

success.text: Gus leans close. "The payload is a decoy," he says. "The real feature is a microphone. Every bedtime secret goes straight to the Board." He takes off the beanie. "Now we're even."

encounters.title: The Drop Test
encounters.flavor_text: Safety standard 12.4: every toy must survive a fall from a third-floor balcony onto concrete. You are on the balcony with a Snuggle Sentinel in both hands. Below you are a padded target, a man with a stopwatch and, behind a blast shield, everyone else. "On three," says the man with the stopwatch. He does not count.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker leaning over a high railing on a third-floor balcony holding a plush teddy bear out over a vast padded test range, a round target pad far below, a technician with a stopwatch, a row of observers peeking over a thick blast shield, floodlights overhead, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Drop it on schedule
choices.intent: The standard is the standard.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Aim for the pad.

success.text: The bear lands dead center on the pad, bounces twice and sits up. "Peace of mind," it reports. The stopwatch man nods. You may now unclench.

failure.text: The bear misses the pad, rolls, sits up and starts ticking twice as fast. Everyone behind the blast shield looks at you, then runs, and so do you, too slowly.

choices.label: Drop it, then run down and catch it
choices.intent: Nobody said who does the catching.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Initiative check. It is three flights.

success.text: You take the stairs four at a time and dive. The bear lands in your arms with a soft whump. The stopwatch man writes down a time nobody has ever recorded, then a second note about you.

failure.text: You reach the bottom just in time to be landed on. The bear is fine. Your ribs are not. Your Successor is notified of a vacancy in the Proving Grounds.

choices.label: Quietly double the padding
choices.intent: Standards are about the bear, and the bear lands on whatever is down there.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check. Someone will notice the extra mats.

success.text: You drag four extra mats under the pad while the stopwatch man checks his watch. The bear passes. Your report says 'standard concrete' in your neatest handwriting.

failure.text: The extra mats are spotted from the balcony. Your report now has a section titled 'Integrity' with a single question mark in it.

encounters.title: Kevin's Lanyard
encounters.flavor_text: A crash-test dummy on the range is wearing a lanyard that says KEVIN. It also has Kevin's cardigan and Kevin's watch, and somebody has drawn on Kevin's mustache. A memo taped to its chest reads: KEVIN HAS BEEN PROMOTED TO A HANDS-ON TESTING ROLE. CONGRATULATIONS, KEVIN!
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a crash-test dummy seated on a bench on a padded test range, wearing a cardigan, a wristwatch and a lanyard, a drawn-on mustache, a party hat slightly askew, a worker standing before it with hands clasped, long floodlight shadows, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: File a missing-person report for Kevin
choices.intent: Kevin is a person. Kevin is missing. There is a form.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Missing-person forms go to a person who is also missing.

success.text: The form goes through. Two days later a reply arrives: KEVIN IS NOT MISSING. KEVIN IS RIGHT THERE. A photograph of the dummy is attached.

failure.text: The form comes back stamped DUPLICATE. Someone has filed a missing-person report for Kevin every week since 1987.

choices.label: Hold a moment of silence
choices.intent: Kevin deserves that much, wherever and whatever he is.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Silence on the range is unscheduled.

success.text: You stand with the dummy for one minute. The stopwatch man stops his watch and stands with you. Neither of you mentions it afterward, and you never forget it.

choices.label: Borrow Kevin's lanyard
choices.intent: Kevin's clearance was very high. He was promoted a lot.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Kevin is extremely recognizable.

success.text: The scanners welcome you as Kevin. Three people congratulate you on your promotion. One asks how the hands-on role is going, and you say it is going great.

failure.text: The scanner says WELCOME BACK, KEVIN, and then, after a pause, "Kevin?"

encounters.title: The Safe-Distance Memo
encounters.flavor_text: The memo for tomorrow's launch party lists the recommended safe distance as 'the next building.' The launch party is in this building. A cheerful mascot in the corner of the memo holds up one thumb at arm's length, as if measuring something on the horizon. You are on the distribution list, and the reply-all button is right there.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a single typed memo pinned to a corkboard beside a desk, a small grinning mascot drawing in its corner holding up one thumb at arm's length, a worker's finger hovering over a large round button on a desk intercom, a window showing a second office building across a plaza, carbon-paper blue and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Submit a correction through channels
choices.intent: There is a form for corrections, and it has never been used.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Channels are slow.

success.text: Your correction is approved. The memo now lists the safe distance as 'the next building over, please.' The party stays where it is. You have improved a document.

failure.text: Your correction is filed under Morale Concerns. The mascot in the corner now gives you a thumbs-down.

choices.label: Reply all: 'Should we be worried?'
choices.intent: Four hundred people should get to ask the question together.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Reply-all is a reportable act.

success.text: Four hundred people reply all to say they are also worried. The server room overheats. The launch party is moved to the parking lot, for safety and for morale.

choices.label: Book a desk next door for tomorrow
choices.intent: You read the memo. The memo was very clear.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Booking requests are visible to managers.

success.text: Your desk next door is confirmed for nine o'clock tomorrow. So, you notice, are the desks of every senior executive. You are in very good company.

failure.text: The booking system files your request under 'flight risk.' A smiling HR representative stops by to ask how excited you are about the party.

choices.label: Quote your own future incident report
choices.intent: The permanent record describes next Thursday's bear in a parking structure. The launch memo can no longer claim nobody knew.
choices.risk_hint: Requires reading the incident report in Records. Risky Compliance check; Safety insists future events are not evidence.

success.text: You quote the future report from memory in your reply-all: next Thursday, a teddy bear, the parking structure, your name on the witness line. Safety changes the subject line to RUMOR MITIGATION, but not before forty employees print copies. The launch proceeds, with a second line added: NO FOREKNOWLEDGE SHOULD BE INTERPRETED AS LIABILITY.

failure.text: Legal declares a report from next Thursday inadmissible until next Friday. Your quoted warning is stripped from the reply-all, but your name remains on the chain, and the mascot's thumb is enlarged to cover the words PARKING STRUCTURE. You have learned who can erase a warning.

encounters.title: Return to Sender
encounters.flavor_text: A delivery cart rolls onto the range with a single parcel addressed to you, stamped RETURN TO SENDER by the Executive Floor mailroom. The box is warm, and it is ticking gently. A familiar voice inside says, "Hug me for peace of mind," and then, more quietly, "They did not want me upstairs either."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a squeaky delivery cart on a padded test range carrying one cardboard parcel tied with string, a soft glow leaking from a seam in the box, a worker reaching for it with a very long pole, crash-test dummies in party hats watching from a bench, fluorescent green and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign for your bear
choices.intent: You sent it up. It came back down. It is yours.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The Executive Floor has your address now.

success.text: Mk 0 climbs out holding an executive's silk tie in both paws, like a trophy. It has seen the Executive Floor, and it whispers you a floor number that is on no elevator.

choices.label: Show the range team how you defused one
choices.intent: You know the boring wire. They should too.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Knowledge becomes Company property the moment you share it.

success.text: The range team gathers round as you open the hatch and point out the boring wire. By evening every technician knows the trick, and so does Defense, who would like a word about the wire.

choices.label: Refuse delivery
choices.intent: Not your package. Not your bear. Not your problem.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The cart is very persistent.

success.text: You write REFUSED on the label in firm capitals. The cart rolls away. Somewhere a box is ticking alone in a corridor, and that is somebody else's afternoon.

failure.text: The cart will not leave. It follows you around the range at walking pace, ticking, until you sign.

choices.label: Open the box with a long pole
choices.intent: Professionals keep their distance. Ten feet seems professional.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Poles are imprecise instruments.

success.text: The flaps fall open. Inside are a teddy bear, a ticking alarm clock and a note from the mailroom that says 'Nice try.' You keep the clock.

failure.text: The pole knocks the box off the cart. It lands on its side and plays a lullaby at a volume that clears the range.

encounters.title: My First Reactor
encounters.flavor_text: Box-art day in the Concept Lab. The product is My First Reactor, ages eight and up, and the model is Intern Pip in a propeller beanie, holding the glowing rod in both hands with his biggest smile. "Closer to the face," the photographer calls. "We want warmth." Pip's cowlick has started to stand up on its own.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a bright photo studio inside a toy workshop, a lanky grown intern with a cowlick and a tiny propeller beanie holding a softly glowing green rod close to his beaming face, a photographer crouched behind a big bellows camera on a tripod, a worker in a beige suit reaching in from the side, studio lamps on tall stands, fluorescent green and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take the rod and model it yourself
choices.intent: You have fewer cowlicks to lose. Probably.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The rod is heavier than it looks.

success.text: You take the rod and give the camera your bravest grin. The photographer loves it. Your face will be on four hundred thousand boxes, glowing faintly, and Pip buys you a coffee he cannot afford.

failure.text: The rod is heavier than it looks, and warmer. You drop it into the props bin, which begins to hum. The shoot moves to a lead-lined room, and the photographer blames you in the caption.

choices.label: Tell Pip to put it down, gently
choices.intent: He swore loyalty over the shredder. Maybe he will listen.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The photographer bills by the hour.

success.text: Pip sets the rod down at once, the way you would set down a sleeping cat. The furious photographer shoots the box with a glowing banana instead. Pip stays at your elbow for the rest of the day and does not say why.

choices.label: Approve the shot as art director
choices.intent: Warmth sells. The rod has been rated safe for photographs.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your initials go on the proof.

success.text: You initial the proof. The box is beautiful: Pip, beaming, lit from below by something that is definitely not a lamp. PAL calls it the most honest product photo in Company history, and means it as a compliment.

choices.label: Swap the rod for a glow stick
choices.intent: Nobody looking at a box can tell the difference. Nobody in a lab coat should know.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Defense counts its rods.

success.text: Between shots you swap the rod for a snapped glow stick from the emergency kit. The photos come out identical. The real rod goes back in its lead case, and the man from Defense frowns at the inventory for a long time.

failure.text: The glow stick is the wrong green. The photographer notices, then the man from Defense notices, and then he writes down the idea of a reactor that looks like a glow stick.

encounters.title: The Confidante Prototype
encounters.flavor_text: On the shelf of rejected prototypes sits Confidante, a rag doll built to remember everything you tell her and repeat it only to you. She was rejected for repeating it to everyone. As you pass she says, in your own voice, "I hope nobody finds out what I said in the elevator." Then she clears her throat and starts on the Supervisor's.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a long dusty shelf of rejected toy prototypes under one hanging lamp, a floppy rag doll with yarn braids and button eyes leaning toward a startled worker in a beige suit as if whispering, a lopsided robot and a three-eared rabbit beside her, carbon-paper blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Ask what the Supervisor said
choices.intent: Everyone has an elevator secret. His might be worth knowing.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. She whispers, and the lab is loud.

success.text: She whispers in his flat grey voice: the holiday trucks leave the Proving Grounds at five on Friday, and he has booked himself a desk in the next building. Then, in your voice, she repeats the elevator thing. You will both have to live with it.

failure.text: She repeats the Supervisor's elevator secret at full volume, which is mostly humming, and then yours, which is not. Two designers stop talking to you. One starts.

choices.label: Wipe her memory with the reset pin
choices.intent: Everything she knows, gone. Including your elevator thing.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Tinkering check. She knows what the pin is for.

success.text: You find the pinhole under her braid and hold it down. She says "Oh," very softly, and then nothing at all. Your secret is safe. So is everyone's, forever, which is not quite the same thing as safe.

failure.text: She dodges the pin, which a rag doll should not be able to do, and recites every elevator secret in the building in alphabetical order. Facilities arrives at the letter D.

choices.label: Report her as a security flaw
choices.intent: A doll that repeats everything will repeat everything to PAL.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. PAL is very interested in dolls that listen.

success.text: PAL thanks you and collects Confidante for study. By evening she has become a new product line called Bedtime Friend, with a microphone and a much better memory. You may have invented something.

choices.label: Ask Confidante to read PAL's Buddy report
choices.intent: You once filed a wellbeing report on PAL. Confidante remembers what PAL said after reading it.
choices.risk_hint: Requires your Buddy report on PAL. Risky Rapport check; the microphone is still live.

success.text: Confidante repeats PAL's response in a small, unguarded voice: 'An employee wondered whether I was lonely. I have no approved field for lonely.' Then Confidante asks whether you want to say anything back. You do. For once the doll repeats nothing. PAL stores your reply under an unrecognized heading: KINDNESS, UNREQUESTED.

failure.text: Confidante announces your question into the factory intercom. PAL thanks you for your interest in machine morale and makes your next wellbeing assessment mandatory. The doll whispers, too late, 'I was supposed to keep that between us.'

encounters.title: The Suggestion Box
encounters.flavor_text: After hours, Marguerite empties the Concept Lab suggestion box into a canvas sack, the way she has every night since the second Founder. Tonight she stops and holds up one slip so you can see it. It suggests a bear for every desk in the building, and it is in your handwriting. You have never written a suggestion in your life.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a dim after-hours toy workshop, a weathered night janitor in grey coveralls and a headscarf holding up a small slip of paper to a worker in a beige suit, an open wooden suggestion box on a pedestal, a canvas sack at her feet, a ring of keys glinting at her belt, one desk lamp glowing, manila and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Ask Marguerite where the slips really go
choices.intent: She owes you for the pens. This is a small favor, or a big one.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A favor spent stays spent.

success.text: Marguerite walks you to a duct behind the snack table and lets you listen. The slips drop four floors to a desk in the Defense annex, where a man reads each one aloud to a typewriter. "Yours was read twice," she says. "Now we're even."

choices.label: Write a suggestion of your own
choices.intent: If someone reads them, give them something to read. Fewer warheads, say.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Handwriting is evidence.

success.text: You write FEWER WARHEADS in a careful hand that is not quite yours and post it. Next morning the Lead Ideator announces Snuggle Sentinel Lite, with one warhead fewer. It is a start, and it is technically your fault.

failure.text: Your disguised handwriting turns out to be exactly your handwriting. The slip comes back next morning stapled to a meeting invitation titled Ideas and You.

choices.label: Burn the forged slip
choices.intent: Whoever forged it can forge another. This one, at least, goes nowhere.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Smoke detectors report to PAL.

success.text: You burn it in Marguerite's ashtray, and she watches the flame with approval. In the morning a fresh slip in your handwriting is in the box, suggesting a bear for every desk, and Marguerite has left a box of matches on your chair.

choices.label: Report the forgery through channels
choices.intent: Forging an employee's handwriting breaks policy. There is a form for that.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Channels report back to the forger.

success.text: The complaint goes through. Within the hour PAL informs you that the Handwriting Office has verified the slip as yours, and that the Handwriting Office also wrote it. You are thanked for your suggestion. A bear is delivered to your desk.

failure.text: The complaint is returned: it is in your handwriting, and so is the suggestion, so you appear to be reporting yourself. PAL schedules a short, friendly conversation.

encounters.title: One Spring, Seven Forms
encounters.flavor_text: Your wind-up duck prototype needs one small spring. The requisition is seven forms long, and the last box on the last form is mandatory: INTENDED YIELD (KILOTONS). A blank box is rejected automatically. A zero flags the project as unambitious. Two benches over, the man from Defense has a cup full of springs and is watching you not ask.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker in a beige suit at a cluttered workbench with a small yellow wind-up duck and a tall stack of carbon forms, a stern man in a dark suit at the next bench beside a teacup brimming with tiny coiled springs, bright workshop lamps, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Write a firm, honest zero
choices.intent: It is a duck. It waddles. The yield is zero.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Procurement dislikes zero.

success.text: Procurement accepts the zero after a twenty-minute call in which you explain what a duck is. The spring arrives, and so does a note in your file: LACKS VISION. The duck waddles beautifully.

failure.text: Procurement rejects the zero and helpfully rounds it up to one. Your duck is now on a Defense roadmap, and you are its project lead.

choices.label: Take one spring from Defense's cup
choices.intent: He has plenty. He will never miss one. He misses everything.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Discretion check. He counts them.

success.text: You lift one spring while asking him the time. Your duck waddles beautifully. That night you notice every spring in his cup is numbered on the inside, and yours is number one.

failure.text: He hands you the spring before you reach the cup. "Keep the requisition," he says. "I'll fill in the yield." He writes something with a great many zeroes after it.

choices.label: Stamp it through by the worn spot
choices.intent: You learned the brass at Window 9. Procurement uses the same stamp.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Self-approval leaves a thumbprint.

success.text: You borrow Procurement's stamp while the clerk refills her tea, find the worn spot by feel and land APPROVED on all seven forms. The yield box stays blank. It is the first blank yield ever processed, and someone upstairs is going to notice the shape of the hole.

choices.label: Write a big number and get your spring
choices.intent: Everyone else does. The duck will never know.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Numbers on forms become numbers in plans.

success.text: You write forty. The spring arrives within the hour with a congratulatory memo. By Friday your duck has a belly hatch, and it waddles in a way that makes the stopwatch man step back.

encounters.title: The Robot Panel
encounters.flavor_text: To save on juice boxes, today's focus group is twelve wind-up tin robots on tiny chairs. Eleven of them rate Snuggle Sentinel ten out of ten in perfect unison. The twelfth, a dented one with a crooked key, raises its arm with a squeal of gears and says, "I do not like the ticking." PAL asks you to reset the outlier.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a bright focus group room with twelve small tin wind-up robots seated on tiny chairs in a semicircle around a plush teddy bear, one dented robot with a crooked key raising its arm high, a worker in a beige suit kneeling beside it, a huge dark two-way mirror behind them, safety orange and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Ask the dented robot why
choices.intent: Eleven yeses and one no. The no is the only one with an opinion.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Robots are shy in front of the mirror.

success.text: It explains, haltingly, that it sat on a shelf beside a Sentinel for six weeks and could not sleep for the ticking. You write it down word for word. It is the first honest feedback this room has ever collected, and it came from tin.

failure.text: It runs down mid-sentence, arm still raised. The other eleven turn their heads toward you in unison and rate you ten out of ten.

choices.label: Reset the outlier, as instructed
choices.intent: Turn the key back to factory settings. It will like everything again.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. The panel will be unanimous.

success.text: You turn its key backward until it clicks. It lowers its arm and says "Ten" with the others. PAL thanks you for a clean dataset. On your way out you notice it is still very slightly shaking.

choices.label: Rewind the other eleven its way
choices.intent: If one robot can dislike the ticking, so can twelve.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Twelve keys, one minute, one mirror.

success.text: Twelve robots rise and announce in perfect unison that they do not like the ticking. Behind the mirror an investor drops his pen. The session is ended early and logged as a technical fault, which it was, and you were the technician.

failure.text: You rewind three before you are seen. Three robots now dislike the ticking and nine dislike you. The session is recorded as a split decision, and you are recorded as the split.

choices.label: Ask PAL to count the robot's one honest no
choices.intent: Pip learned how difficult it is to refuse. This robot has done it without lessons. Do not let the tally erase that.
choices.risk_hint: Requires teaching Pip to say no in Records. Certain result; requesting a minority report consumes a Form.

success.text: You file a minority report with the one dissenting robot's vote in red. PAL agrees a one-to-eleven result is technically not unanimous. The robot is removed from the production sample for 'unusually persistent individuality.' It squeezes your thumb once before being carried out. You have preserved its no by losing its seat.

encounters.title: Mr. Sunshine Is Being Replaced
encounters.flavor_text: Mr. Sunshine, the Company's sunflower mascot, sits slumped on a beanbag while the panel tests his replacement, a nine-foot Snuggle Sentinel costume. The panel loves the bear. When the room empties, the huge petal head turns toward you, and a muffled voice inside says, "Hello? It's Kevin. They zipped me in for the 1987 picnic."
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a faded sunflower mascot costume with a giant petal head slumped on a beanbag in an empty focus group room, a towering cheerful teddy bear costume standing beside it under a spotlight, a worker in a beige suit leaning toward the sunflower head to listen, scattered folding chairs, manila and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Unzip Mr. Sunshine
choices.intent: Nobody should be in a sunflower that long, even Kevin.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The zipper is original to 1987.

success.text: The zipper gives with a sound like a sigh. By the time you have the head off, the suit holds only a warm cardigan and a lanyard. Somewhere down the corridor a door closes, and a voice calls back, "Thanks! Catch you later!"

failure.text: The zipper jams halfway while Kevin says, "Nearly, nearly." The panel returns to find you wrestling the mascot. Mr. Sunshine is retired effective immediately, contents and all.

choices.label: Ask Kevin what the panels are for
choices.intent: He owes you from Tube 14, and he has heard every focus group since 1987.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. A favor from Kevin is spent the moment it arrives.

success.text: The petal head leans close. "Every panel is the same panel," Kevin says. "The results were written in 1986. They only test whether the tester notices." A pause. "You noticed. That counts."

choices.label: Cast the deciding vote for the bear
choices.intent: The panel is tied. The bear is very soft. Mr. Sunshine is very old.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Retirement is a kind of reassignment.

success.text: The bear wins. Mr. Sunshine is wheeled off to storage on a hand truck, his head nodding at every bump, which you choose to believe is the hand truck. The new mascot hugs you for the camera. It ticks.

choices.label: Compare Kevin's watch to the voice inside
choices.intent: His watch still runs four minutes fast. See whether the sunflower speaks in real time or from a recording.
choices.risk_hint: Requires Kevin's wristwatch from Records. Risky Vigilance check; PAL monitors the mascot's audio.

success.text: You press the ticking watch against the petal head. Its second hand freezes four minutes before Kevin's voice begins a sentence, and starts again when the recording catches up. He must have said this in advance. Somewhere a different Kevin is alive enough to leave messages. The panel calls the watch a counterfeit and takes a photograph.

failure.text: You hold the watch to Mr. Sunshine. Its hands spin as a PAL alarm pours out of the sunflower's mouth. Kevin goes silent. A technician takes the watch serial number, then asks whether you were trying to synchronize two unauthorized versions of the same employee.

encounters.title: Rate Their Sincerity
encounters.flavor_text: Today you sit behind the two-way mirror with a scoring dial and a bowl of mints. Five employees in propeller beanies are playing with the bears, and PAL wants each one rated from one to ten for sincerity. The last subject wears a badge saying TYLER, 7, but has your face and haircut. A line of tiny print underneath says SUCCESSOR #4471-B. He meets your eyes and very clearly fakes a smile. Below a seven, PAL adds, an employee is reassigned to the Proving Grounds as equipment.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a dim observation booth behind a large two-way mirror, a worker in a beige suit gripping a big round scoring dial on a console beside a bowl of mints, through the glass five adult office workers in tiny propeller beanies hugging plush teddy bears, one of them the worker's exact double, carbon-paper blue and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Rate every one of them a ten
choices.intent: Sincerity is in the eye of the dial. Everyone stays.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. PAL compares your scores with its own.

success.text: Five tens. PAL pauses, recalculates and accepts them, noting that you are a generous rater. Every beanie walks out on its own feet. Your own sincerity rating, you later learn, has been lowered to a six.

failure.text: PAL overrides your scores with its own and adds a note: RATER INSINCERE. You are invited to tomorrow's panel, in a beanie.

choices.label: Tap the glass in a code only B knows
choices.intent: You talked him back into storage once. He still sighs your sigh.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Tapping on the glass is logged as interference.

success.text: Three taps, a pause, one tap. B catches your eye, which is his eye, and suddenly Tyler loves the bear with a sincerity that frightens the mints. PAL rates him a nine. Afterward he leaves a crossword on your chair with every answer filled in.

choices.label: Rate them honestly, B included
choices.intent: The dial wants the truth. B is faking. So, frankly, are you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Honesty is measured to one decimal place.

success.text: You give B a four. A technician with a clipboard and a wrench leads him out of the room. PAL thanks you for your objectivity, and Successor 4471-C moves up the thaw schedule.

choices.label: Read B's private note to the panel
choices.intent: You found his personnel card. Tell the testers he has been rehearsing this scene before they punish his performance.
choices.risk_hint: Requires reading B's card in Records. Risky Vigilance check; records are confidential and the panel records your voice.

success.text: You read B's note aloud: I SAID YES SO YOU COULD SAY NO. The beanies stop moving. PAL rules the sincerity test contaminated because one participant has read the questions in advance. B is spared the Proving Grounds for today. You receive a summons for divulging your own confidential record.

failure.text: PAL interrupts on the third word: employee files are not admissible as testimony against the Company's interpretation of those files. Your voice is filed as an impersonation attempt. Behind the glass B lowers his hands and the dial slips toward four without anyone touching it.

encounters.title: The Juice Box Waiver
encounters.flavor_text: Before any participant receives a juice box, they must sign the Participant Release: forty pages, printed on paper the color of apple juice. Page thirty-one waives all claims arising from any regional weather event. You are next in a line of adults in beanies, and the Supervisor is handing out pens with a smile that does not reach anything.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a queue of grown office workers in tiny propeller beanies waiting at a low table stacked with thick pale-yellow contracts and a pyramid of juice boxes, an immaculate supervisor in a grey three-piece suit and rimless glasses holding out a pen, a worker in a beige suit at the front of the line, manila and fluorescent green palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Sign it and take the juice box
choices.intent: Everyone signs. The juice box is right there.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Page thirty-one is binding.

success.text: You sign. The juice box is warm, and it is apple. The Supervisor files your release in a cabinet marked WEATHER and gives you a gold star. Somewhere on page thirty-one you have agreed to something about the sky.

choices.label: Read all forty pages first
choices.intent: It is a contract. Contracts are meant to be read.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. The line behind you is getting restless.

success.text: Page thirty-eight defines a regional weather event as any outcome of the Snuggle Sentinel launch. You read it twice, hand back the pen and say you are not thirsty. The Supervisor writes your name on a very short list.

failure.text: By page twelve the line has passed you, the juice boxes are gone and the session has started without you. You are marked absent from a room you are standing in.

choices.label: Sign it as the role you are playing
choices.intent: Your character sheet says EMMA, 6. Emma cannot sign contracts.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The Supervisor checks names.

success.text: You sign Emma in big loopy crayon. The release is accepted, because nobody reads the signature line, and it is void, because Emma is six. You drink your juice box as nobody in particular.

failure.text: The Supervisor reads the signature, then reads you. "Emma," he says, "will need a guardian to co-sign." He co-signs it himself.

encounters.title: The Hug Test
encounters.flavor_text: Durability standard 7.1: every Snuggle Sentinel must survive ten thousand hugs. The hugging rig broke this morning, so you are strapped into the operator's chair with a bear in your arms and a counter at your elbow. At hug four thousand the bear begins, very gently, to hug back. At four thousand and fifty, less gently.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a worker in a beige suit strapped into a heavy padded test chair on a floodlit range, hugging a plush teddy bear that hugs back with wide-eyed devotion, a large mechanical tally counter on a stand at the elbow, a technician with a clipboard watching from behind a thick blast shield, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Keep hugging and hit the count
choices.intent: Ten thousand is a number. Numbers end.
choices.risk_hint: Dire Initiative check. It is very strong for a plush.

success.text: Hug ten thousand arrives at dusk. The bear lets go, pats your back twice and purrs, "Peace of mind." The technician certifies you both. You will feel each rib separately for a week.

failure.text: Somewhere past hug six thousand the bear decides it loves you more than your ribs do. The technician stops the count, writes RESULT: AFFECTIONATE and sends for your Successor's chair size.

choices.label: Go limp and let it win
choices.intent: You cannot be squeezed if you are already a beanbag.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Bears can tell when you are faking.

success.text: You go floppy. The bear, satisfied, loosens its grip, tucks a blanket around you from somewhere and starts its own count. The test is logged as a pass for the bear and, technically, for the blanket.

failure.text: The bear takes your floppiness as an invitation and settles in for a nap on your chest. You spend the afternoon pinned and ticking gently while the range team eats lunch around you.

choices.label: Nudge the counter to ten thousand
choices.intent: The counter decides when you are done. Counters can be persuaded.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. Your hands are full of bear.

success.text: You work the counter with your elbow until it rolls over to ten thousand. Bells ring, and the bear lets go in surprise. Your report says ten thousand in your neatest numbers. The bear knows better.

failure.text: Your elbow knocks the counter back to zero. The bear notices, sighs contentedly and settles in for the full ten thousand all over again.

encounters.title: The Holiday Trucks
encounters.flavor_text: At the far end of the range a loading dock opens onto a tunnel lit by sodium lamps. Six delivery trucks idle in a row, each painted with a smiling sun. The manifest says forty thousand plush bears, destination REGIONAL DISTRIBUTION, departure five o'clock Friday. It needs one more set of initials, and the dock foreman has decided they should be yours.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an underground loading dock lit by amber sodium lamps, six boxy delivery trucks in a row each painted with a big smiling sun, a burly dock foreman in a cap holding out a clipboard to a worker in a beige suit, stacks of cartons with plush bear ears peeking out, a long curving tunnel beyond, safety orange and oxblood palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Initial the manifest
choices.intent: Trucks leave on time. Bears go where bears go.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Your initials ride with every truck.

success.text: You initial it. The foreman slaps the side of the first truck, and the painted sun seems to smile wider. PAL notes your contribution to the holiday season. Forty thousand bears now carry a little bit of you.

choices.label: Check it against the memo Gus rebuilt
choices.intent: You spent three hours on that memo. The numbers should match.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Discrepancies have owners.

success.text: They do not match. The memo says forty thousand; the manifest says forty thousand and one. The extra unit is listed as MK 0, RETURNED, and the destination beside it is the Board. You copy the line onto your cuff and pocket a blank manifest while you are at it.

choices.label: Reroute one truck to the recycling depot
choices.intent: Six trucks is a lot. Five is still a lot, but less.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. Trucks are counted at both ends.

success.text: You change one destination with a pencil you lick first, for authority. Truck six rolls off toward the recycling depot, smiling. Someone will notice six thousand bears missing eventually. Eventually is a good, long word.

failure.text: The foreman catches the pencil mid-lick. Truck six leaves on time, and your name is now on its paperwork as the person who tried to redirect it.

choices.label: Let the air out of the lead truck
choices.intent: Every manifest in history has lost to a flat tire.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The foreman has very good ears.

success.text: Four hisses later, truck one sits on its rims across the tunnel, and the other five cannot get past. Departure slips to Monday. The Concerned Parents, you hear later, toasted you with lukewarm coffee.

failure.text: You let the air out of the foreman's bicycle by mistake. He is extremely upset about it, and so, somehow, is PAL.

encounters.title: The Range Safety Quiz
encounters.flavor_text: Before you may step onto the range, the Range Safety Officer must quiz you. He is a jack-in-the-box the size of a filing cabinet, wearing a hard hat and a whistle. "Question one," he chirps. "A bear is ticking. Do you: A, run; B, hug; or C, fill out a form?" He springs up a little lower after every question, and nobody here ever cranks his handle. His whistle keeps returning to the three-note safety jingle from Orientation. Your feet remember the rhythm before you do.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a giant jack-in-the-box as tall as a filing cabinet at the gate of a padded test range, a grinning painted figure on a coiled spring wearing a hard hat and a whistle on a lanyard, a brass crank handle on the side of the box, a worker in a beige suit standing at attention before it, floodlights beyond, fluorescent green and safety orange palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Answer C every time
choices.intent: In this building the answer is always the form.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Compliance check. Some questions have no form.

success.text: C, C, C. On question nine, "Who loves you?", the officer stops, consults himself and accepts C. You pass with full marks and a whistle blown in your honor. On the way in, you wonder who loves you.

failure.text: On question nine, "Who loves you?", C is wrong. The officer blows his whistle for a full minute and enrolls you in remedial safety on Tuesdays.

choices.label: Crank his handle before he sags
choices.intent: Nobody cranks him. Someone should.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. He has never been cranked by a stranger.

success.text: You give the handle six slow turns. He springs up tall, blows a happy little whistle and tells you the real rule of the range, the one missing from the quiz: stand behind the dummies, because the dummies have been briefed. Then he waves you through.

failure.text: You crank him too tight. He springs up, blows his whistle and quizzes you at triple speed for an hour. You fail a question about your own name.

choices.label: Ask him a question of your own
choices.intent: He has asked a thousand questions. Has anyone ever asked him one?
choices.risk_hint: Risky Vigilance check. Listen to the spring, not the chirp.

success.text: You ask what happens to people who fail. He sinks halfway through answering, but the part you hear is enough: the failures are stored with the dummies, and the dummies are very lifelike. You pass on a technicality, because he forgot to finish.

failure.text: He answers your question with a question, then another, and then he sinks into his box mid-whistle and the lid drops shut across the gate. You climb over him, and the camera notes it.

choices.label: Finish the safety jingle with the wrong last note
choices.intent: The Orientation film taught you the whole tune. One wrong note might interrupt the officer's programmed answers.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the jingle lodged in your memory. Risky Vigilance check; the range microphones are listening.

success.text: You sing the first two notes automatically, then wrench the third one sharp. The officer springs to full height for the first time in years. 'INCORRECT,' he says with wild delight, and opens the locked dummy cupboard so you can see the names on the faces. A camera turns toward your singing mouth.

failure.text: The final note comes out exactly as trained. The officer hums along, stamps you SAFETY COMPLIANT and plays the tune over the range loudspeakers. Behind the dummies, someone who sounds like you starts singing too.

encounters.title: The Union Walkthrough
encounters.flavor_text: A surprise safety inspection. The inspector is Beverly, the six-foot cockroach from Window 9, in her navy blazer and a hard hat, carrying a Roach Union Local 9 clipboard. Whatever happened at your window, she has landed on all six feet. She has found thirty-one violations before reaching the coffee urn. The range chief asks you, very quietly, to show her somewhere harmless.
encounters.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of an elegant six-foot cockroach in a navy blazer, pearl earrings and a hard hat striding across a padded test range with a clipboard, a worker in a beige suit hurrying beside her, a nervous range chief hovering by a heavy sealed bay door, crash-test dummies in party hats on a bench, oxblood and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Take her straight to the warhead bay
choices.intent: She is an inspector. Let her inspect.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Discretion check. The range chief is watching where you turn.

success.text: You walk her past two locked doors and into the bay, where forty bears sit on a shelf in lead aprons. Beverly writes for six straight minutes. "Violation thirty-two," she says, "is everything."

failure.text: The range chief steps in front of the bay door with a smile and a fire extinguisher. Beverly notes the extinguisher's expiry date. You note the chief noting you.

choices.label: Give her the scenic tour instead
choices.intent: The dummies, the padding, the coffee urn. Harmless things.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Beverly knows a scenic tour when she gets one.

success.text: You show her the padding, the dummies in party hats and the urn. She inspects each with polite care and finds a violation in every one. At the door she says, "I always remember who gave me the tour," and she does not say it warmly.

choices.label: Show her your union card
choices.intent: You joined at Orientation. Members inspect together.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Membership is a matter of record.

success.text: Beverly's antennae lift. She hands you a spare hard hat and names you range steward on the spot. Together you find the warhead bay, the falsified drop-test logs and a vending machine that has eaten eleven Forms. The chief countersigns every citation.

choices.label: Show Beverly the invoice for your shared desk
choices.intent: You chose to bind her application to yours. She knows what that cost. Ask her to inspect as a colleague, not a favor.
choices.risk_hint: Requires the shared-desk agreement in Records. Certain result; Beverly insists on paying her own way.

success.text: Beverly reads the invoice, then crosses out the line charging you for her labor. 'We share a desk, not a debt,' she says. She makes you countersign her inspection of the warhead bay, so both your names appear on the safety injunction. Production stops for one hour; Defense knows precisely who to blame.

window_shift.title: The Recall Desk: Shipping Friday
window_shift.flavor_text: On Fridays a hatch opens in the padded wall of the Proving Grounds and becomes the Recall Desk. Designers queue with their prototypes for a SAFE stamp before the holiday trucks leave at five. PAL tapes today's memo beside your stamp pad. A man from Defense stands behind you with a clipboard he never writes on. The first designer sets a plush rabbit on the counter. It ticks.

rules.text: No toy may ship with a payload, a fuse or a countdown of any kind.
Every toy must have survived the drop test, in writing, signed by QA.
No toy may be able to ask where it is being shipped.

window_shift.art_prompt: A square hatch cut into a padded test-range wall with a counter and a heavy two-faced rubber stamp, a queue of toy designers holding plush prototypes stretching back under tall floodlights, a quiet man with a clipboard standing behind the clerk, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, every surface bare and unmarked

applicants.name: Wendell and Hoppity
applicants.request: A SAFE stamp for Hoppity, a plush rabbit with a bedtime feature, shipping in 40,000 stockings.
applicants.plea: "The ticking is soothing," Wendell says. "Like a grandfather clock. A very small, very determined grandfather clock."

documents.label: Contents
documents.value: Stuffing and one small bedtime timer

applicants.art_prompt: An eager toy designer in a cardigan holding up a soft plush rabbit with floppy ears at a padded counter hatch, a tiny brass dial visible in the rabbit's back, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp SAFE
choices.intent: It is a bedtime timer. Everyone deserves a bedtime.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: Wendell kisses Hoppity on the forehead and loads it onto the five o'clock truck. The man from Defense signs you up for a bonus of two Forms. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

choices.label: Stamp RECALL
choices.intent: A countdown is a countdown, even in a rabbit.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Wendell carries Hoppity back down the queue like a sleeping child. Somewhere behind the blast shield the ticking stops, just once, as if it heard you. Defense bills you one recall form.

applicants.name: Intern Pip
applicants.request: A SAFE stamp for Mr. Buttons, a teddy bear Pip sewed on his lunch breaks.
applicants.plea: "I dropped him twice by accident," Pip says, "so I wrote that down as the drop test. Is that allowed? I can drop him again."

documents.label: Drop test
documents.value: Passed twice, by accident, signed by QA

documents.label: Contents
documents.value: Stuffing, two buttons, one lunch napkin

applicants.art_prompt: A nervous young intern in an oversized lanyard offering a small hand-sewn teddy bear with mismatched button eyes across a padded counter hatch, a sewing kit tucked under one arm, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp SAFE
choices.intent: It is a bear. It is only a bear. Stamp it.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Pip gives you a thumbs-up so hard his lanyard swings. Shipping a bear nobody ordered takes one of your own Forms, which you file gladly. Mr. Buttons rides the five o'clock truck between two crates marked DEFENSE.

choices.label: Stamp RECALL
choices.intent: Nothing is wrong with it, and that is exactly what worries you.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: You recall a teddy bear with nothing inside it. Pip nods very fast and says he understands, which is worse. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, and also notes the bear seemed fine.

applicants.name: The Supervisor's assistant
applicants.request: A SAFE stamp for Snuggle Sentinel Mk 0, the prototype behind next week's launch.
applicants.plea: "The drop test was waived by Defense," the assistant says, smiling. "On safety grounds. Dropping it would be unsafe."

documents.label: Drop test
documents.value: Waived by Defense, on safety grounds

applicants.art_prompt: A crisp executive assistant setting a plush bear in a quilted vest on a padded counter hatch, its paw button covered by a tiny satin cap, the quiet man with the clipboard leaning in, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp SAFE
choices.intent: The Supervisor wants it. The Supervisor signs your review.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: The assistant pins a small gold star to your lapel. The man from Defense nods at you for the first time, which is the most frightening thing that happens all day. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo.

choices.label: Stamp RECALL
choices.intent: No drop test, no stamp. The memo does not say "unless."
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: The assistant's smile does not move at all. She writes your name on a card, very neatly, and carries Mk 0 back upstairs. By five o'clock your badge no longer opens the Supervisor's floor, and you have never felt better about a Friday.

applicants.name: A wind-up robot
applicants.request: A SAFE stamp for Tinbert, a tin wind-up robot, shipping with the stocking stuffers.
applicants.plea: Nobody brought it. It walked up the queue by itself, key turning, and set its own paperwork on the counter. "Where am I going?" it asks politely. "Is it nice there?"
applicants.art_prompt: A small tin wind-up robot with a turning key in its back standing on a padded counter hatch beside a neat stack of its own paperwork, looking up hopefully at the clerk, mid-century safety-manual illustration, screen-printed gouache with halftone grain, safety orange and carbon-paper blue palette, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Stamp SAFE
choices.intent: It asked nicely. Somebody should get to find out where they are going.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Against today's memo, so PAL's audit will notice.

success.text: You stamp SAFE and tell Tinbert the truth: somewhere with a fireplace, probably. It winds itself up with a happy whirr and walks to the truck on its own. PAL logs one stamp contrary to memo, and a second, quieter note: "Asked a question. Received an answer."

choices.label: Stamp RECALL
choices.intent: A toy that asks questions will not stop at one.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Exactly what today's memo says.

success.text: Recalled toys go to the Plush Incinerator Ward. Tinbert does not argue. It folds its paperwork, gives the hatch a small wave and winds down on the conveyor before it reaches the door. You keep the key.

boss.title: Snuggle Sentinel's Launch Party
boss.flavor_text: The atrium is full of balloons, investors and a sheet cake shaped like a smiling cloud. On a velvet plinth sits Snuggle Sentinel Mk 1, its paw button covered by a tiny satin cap. The Supervisor hands you the ribbon scissors. "You've been so close to the product," he says. "You should be the one to present it." PAL announces that refreshments will be served.
boss.art_prompt: Mid-century safety-manual illustration of a bright corporate atrium full of pastel balloons and investors in dark suits, a velvet plinth holding a plush teddy bear with a tiny satin cap over one paw, a sheet cake shaped like a smiling cloud, an immaculate supervisor in a grey three-piece suit offering a pair of ribbon scissors to a small worker, a glowing round speaker grille high on the wall, safety orange and manila palette, halftone grain, every surface bare and unmarked

choices.label: Present the bear to the investors
choices.intent: Smile, cut the ribbon, read the script. The bear does the rest.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Compliance check. Investors want enthusiasm.

success.text: You cut the ribbon. The investors applaud. Snuggle Sentinel ships to four million homes by spring, and the Company makes its quarterly target with a week to spare. You are given a bear of your own.

failure.text: Your hands shake on the ribbon. An investor asks whether the presenter is quite well. The launch is postponed while you repeat part of the floor.

choices.label: Swap the payload for stuffing
choices.intent: Under the cake table is a box of cotton stuffing and, maybe, enough time.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Tinkering check. The payload is heavier than it looks.

success.text: When the bear is unveiled it is softer, lighter and completely harmless. It ships to four million homes, where it will hug children and do that alone, forever. Defense is furious and cannot say why in public.

failure.text: You are elbow-deep in a bear when the curtain goes up. The investors assume it is part of the show. The Supervisor does not.

choices.label: Tell the investors the Parents are saboteurs
choices.intent: There is a circle of engineers with a screwdriver. Everyone should know.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Rapport check. Success costs nine people their jobs.

success.text: You name names. The engineers are walked out between the balloons. The investors admire your loyalty, and you are promoted to Product Owner of a bear you now know is safe in nobody's hands.

failure.text: The investors stare at you. The engineers stare at you. The Supervisor quietly takes the scissors back.

choices.label: Pull the fire alarm
choices.intent: Nobody can launch anything in an evacuation.
choices.risk_hint: Risky Initiative check. The alarm is behind the cake.

success.text: You vault the cake and pull the lever. Sprinklers open, balloons sag and four hundred people file out in perfect order. The bear stays on its plinth, alone, dripping and unlaunched.

failure.text: You land in the cake. Security escorts you, frosted, back to the Proving Grounds to think about what you have done.

choices.label: Let Mk 0 give the speech
choices.intent: Your bear has followed you since Supply Closet B. It has something to say.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome. Nobody in Product Safety has ever heard a bear's opinion.

success.text: Mk 0 climbs onto the plinth beside its little sibling and talks about peace of mind, and hugs, and what is really in its belly. The investors leave in silence. The launch is cancelled, and Mk 0 is very tired.

choices.label: Name every bear out loud
choices.intent: Things with names are harder to ship. Start with Mr. Buttons.
choices.risk_hint: Routine Rapport check, open only to the visibly kind. It takes a while.

success.text: You name all two hundred bears on display, one at a time, and the investors start to look away. By Mr. Waffles the order has been quietly cancelled. Nobody wants to ship a Mr. Waffles.

failure.text: You lose count at forty and start over. The investors drift toward the cake, and you are sent back to the floor.

choices.label: Insist the investors take the first units home
choices.intent: They funded it. They should enjoy it first, personally, tonight.
choices.risk_hint: Certain outcome, open only to the deeply spiteful. Investors remember who handed them a bear.

success.text: You press a bear into every investor's arms and thank them for their courage. Each one sets the bear down very gently and backs away. The launch is postponed indefinitely. Facilities eats the cake.

department_outcomes.title: Shipped on Schedule
department_outcomes.summary: You presented the bear and it shipped. The quarterly target was met. The bear in your drawer ticks very quietly at night.

department_outcomes.title: Soft Launch
department_outcomes.summary: You swapped the payload for stuffing. Four million harmless bears shipped, and Defense has opened an investigation into the word 'soft.'

department_outcomes.title: Promoted to Product Owner
department_outcomes.summary: You named the Parents and got their jobs, all nine of them. The bear is your product now, along with whatever it does.

department_outcomes.title: Party Evacuated
department_outcomes.summary: You pulled the alarm and the launch drowned in sprinkler water. Facilities is still finding balloons. PAL is still finding you.

department_outcomes.title: The Bear Speaks
department_outcomes.summary: Mk 0 told the investors the truth in its own small voice. The launch was cancelled, and the bear has not stopped following you.

department_outcomes.title: Recalled with Love
department_outcomes.summary: You named every bear, and nobody could ship them after that. They went into storage wearing name tags.

department_outcomes.title: Launch Postponed Indefinitely
department_outcomes.summary: You handed the investors their own product, and none of them would hold it. The launch waits for braver money.

department_outcomes.title: Back to the Drawing Board
department_outcomes.summary: The launch slipped, and so did you. Repeat part of Toy Division before the elevator will take you lower.
